clue.text: Ugly house I'd renovated

indicators.note: a house that is renovated is done over, so its letters, with I'd, are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a house they've done up, calling it ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovated' rearranges the seven letters of HOUSE and I'D.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repulsive to look at is ugly in the extreme.

clue.text: Dutch reserve

annotationWithheld.why: Dutch reserve (7): RESERVE fits HUSBAND (to conserve), but 'Dutch' is Cockney slang for wife, not husband; no honest sense of 'Dutch' gives the answer.

clue.text: It produces a positive result from stereoscopic camera

definitions.meaning: in grammar, two negatives cancel to make a positive
a stereo camera produces a pair of film negatives

explanation.surface: A gadget that gets good outcomes from a 3D camera.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatically, two nots cancel to an affirmative; photographically, a twin-lens camera yields paired film images.

clue.text: Likelihood that biblical scholar resides in spacious surroundings

indicators.note: resides in means one piece lives inside the other

parts.note: OS, outsize, means very large; it surrounds the scholar
DD is Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: The chance that a theologian lives in a roomy house.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting chances express how probable something is.

clue.text: Dispatchedeastern currency to solicitor

parts.note: the sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries
a tout is someone who solicits custom

explanation.surface: Foreign money was sent to a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' looks like a lawyer but means someone who solicits, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: Sent away on an errand means dispatched.

clue.text: Financier is given hush money

parts.note: a CA, a chartered accountant, is a money professional, standing in loosely for a financier
SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A money man gets paid to keep quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes and coins in hand are money in its plainest form.

clue.text: Conservative carrying less weight daily

parts.note: leaner means thinner, with less fat

explanation.surface: A Tory politician is slimming down every day.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' is British for a domestic help who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a charwoman who comes in to do housework.

clue.text: Place in an Assisi tea-room

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A spot in a café in the Italian town of Assisi.
explanation.definitionFit: A location or spot is a place.

clue.text: Reduced pictures mounted in attractive frame

indicators.note: a frame goes round a picture, so the word for attractive surrounds the turned piece

parts.note: cute means sweetly attractive

indicators.note: in a down clue mounted means going up, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: art is paintings and pictures

explanation.surface: Discounted pictures are hung in pretty frames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' turns ART into TRA, which goes inside CUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold below the usual price are cheap and marked down.

clue.text: Making another gift of the portrait

explanation.surface: A portrait given away for a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a split word it means giving again; whole, it means a depiction or likeness.

clue.text: Spending on hi-fi represents good value

definitions.meaning: money laid out on audio equipment, read literally
a purchase or stake that pays off well

explanation.surface: Buying expensive stereo gear is said to be money well spent.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally an outlay on audio gear; idiomatically a sensible, profitable outlay.

clue.text: Constantly heartened by Lord Lieutenant being a friend

indicators.note: being heartened by something means having it put at the heart, so one piece is placed in the middle of the other

parts.note: AY (aye) is an old word for always or ever
LL is the abbreviation for Lord Lieutenant

explanation.surface: A county's royal representative proves a constant source of support.
explanation.walkthrough: AY is the poetic 'aye', meaning ever; LL goes in its middle. A Lord Lieutenant is the monarch's representative in a British county.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner or supporter on your side is a friend in this sense.

clue.text: Came upon an empty pool

annotationWithheld.why: Came upon an empty pool (5): FOUND reads as O (empty) inside FUND (pool), but no separate word signals the insertion; 'empty' would have to give O and say where it goes.

clue.text: A recurring melody in opera

indicators.note: recurring here is read as running back again, so the word for melody is read backwards

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: An opera has a tune that keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recurring' turns AIR round to RIA, after A. The whole clue is also the definition: a solo song in an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo song set within an opera is the classic operatic showpiece.

clue.text: Noted performer carrying one instrument

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside, so the performer word contains the numeral

parts.note: a star is a celebrated performer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A famous musician carries one instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-necked Indian lute is a stringed musical instrument.

clue.text: Proudly exhibit a singular wine

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Someone proudly shows off an outstanding wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear or display something ostentatiously is to show it off.

clue.text: He may deal with a cavity first

definitions.text: He may deal with a cavity first

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
1ST, with the figure read as the letter I, is the short form of first

explanation.surface: Someone whose job is treating holes in teeth before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives 1ST, the figure 1 standing in for I. The whole clue also describes the tooth doctor who fills cavities.
explanation.definitionFit: A tooth specialist treats decay holes, so the whole clue describes that professional.

clue.text: Come-back by naval NCO's in formal ceremony

indicators.note: in places the naval rank's letters inside the word for a ceremony

parts.note: a rite is a solemn ceremonial act
PO is petty officer, a naval non-commissioned officer; PO'S gives POS

explanation.surface: Petty officers make a cheeky remark during a solemn naval ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick retort is a verbal come-back in an argument.

clue.text: Drawn from a writer of romance and adventure

definitions.text: a writer of romance and adventure
definitions.meaning: H. Rider ..., author of King Solomon's Mines

explanation.surface: A picture taken from an adventure novelist's book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' looks like a sketch but means tired-looking. Rider Haggard was a Victorian adventure novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn means gaunt and worn; the surname belongs to the author of She and King Solomon's Mines.

clue.text: She is a warm woman

parts.note: to heat is to warm
her is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman is said to be warm-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name stands for a female person, as the pronoun does.

clue.text: Nod and make the delivery

definitions.meaning: to leave something at its destination

explanation.surface: Someone nods along and drops off a parcel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding off is falling asleep; leaving a parcel somewhere is the other sense.

clue.text: And back in fashion for a long time

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for fashion

parts.note: chic means stylish, the height of fashion

indicators.note: back means the word nor is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is back in style and staying put for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NOR into RON, which 'in' puts inside CHIC. The definition is loose: lasting a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: A persistent, long-lasting condition is described as continuing over an extended period.

clue.text: Study a book in relation to its background

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study
a text is a book

explanation.surface: Reading a book with reference to its historical setting.
explanation.definitionFit: The circumstances surrounding an event form its setting or background.

clue.text: Broke down when about to be tortured

parts.note: C is circa, about
racked means put on the rack, tortured

explanation.surface: A prisoner broke when facing torture.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gave way under pressure has broken or split.

clue.text: Dined about noon-or before

indicators.note: about means going round, so the meal word surrounds the letter for midday

parts.note: ate is a synonym for dined

explanation.surface: Someone ate their dinner around midday, or earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Ante is the Latin-derived prefix meaning prior, as in antenatal.

clue.text: Harry is a contemptible fellow

definitions.meaning: to harry is to pursue and pester

explanation.surface: Someone called Harry is a rotter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name, but it is the verb to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to chase relentlessly; an old word for a despicable man is a dog.

clue.text: Prisoner comes back to a celebration

indicators.note: comes back means the word for a convict is read backwards

parts.note: a lag is a convict, especially an old lag

explanation.surface: A convict returns home to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes back' turns LAG into GAL; 'to' joins A on.
explanation.definitionFit: A festive occasion or grand party is a celebration.

clue.text: Roll of notes I found in a river-bed

parts.note: a wad is a bundle of banknotes

explanation.surface: A bundle of money is found in a dry riverbed.
explanation.walkthrough: A wadi is a dry valley in the Middle East or North Africa that floods in the rainy season.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert watercourse that is dry outside the rains is a riverbed.

clue.text: A medical practitioner retired in the end

indicators.note: retired means going back, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: a doc is a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor finally retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns A DOC round to CODA.
explanation.definitionFit: A concluding passage at the close of a musical piece is its end.

clue.text: Need to clear the air and finish off the drumstick

definitions.meaning: to have a grievance to settle with someone
literally, to have the last of the meat left on a chicken leg

explanation.surface: After a row, someone wants to settle things and polish off their chicken leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means holding a grievance to air; literally it means gnawing meat off a joint.

clue.text: Returned the thing following a dispute

indicators.note: returned means the word for the thing is read backwards

parts.note: it is the pronoun for the thing
ff is the abbreviation for following, used of pages

explanation.surface: Someone sent the item back after a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor quarrel is a petty dispute.

clue.text: Educated BR press boss

parts.note: BR was British Rail, which ran the trains
ED is the editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A railway newspaper chief is well schooled.
explanation.walkthrough: BR stands for British Rail, the former UK national railway, so it gives TRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone schooled or taught a skill is educated.
